translationRepairs: Emperor Guangwu went to the post station and said to Ren Guang, "Boqing, we are weak now. I am thinking of throwing in with Chengtou Zilu's and Lizi Du's bands in the city—what do you think?"
Emperor Guangwu went to the post station and said to Ren Guang, "Boqing, we are weak now. I am considering whether we should join the forces of Chengtou Zilu and Lizi Du. What do you think?"
俱 makes the proposed action collective: Guangwu asks whether they should join those forces together.
The Shizu entered the relay inn and said to Guang: "Boqing, our strength is now weak; I wish to join together the troops of Chengtou Zilu and Lizi Du in the city—what of it?"
Shizu entered the relay inn and said to Guang, "Boqing, our strength is now weak. I am considering whether we should join the forces of Chengtou Zilu and Lizi Du. What do you think?"
俱 makes the proposed action collective: Shizu asks whether they should join those forces together.

The Shizu thereupon with Guang and the others entered the borders of Tangyang at dusk, had each rider carry torches so that they filled the marshes; Guang's flames lit heaven and earth, and the whole city was without exception shaken and terrified, and that night it submitted.

The Shizu thereupon with Guang and the others entered the borders of Tangyang at dusk, had each rider carry torches so that they filled the marshes; the bright flames lit heaven and earth, and the whole city was without exception shaken and terrified, and that night it submitted.
In s0022 使騎各持炬火…光炎燭天地, 光炎 is the torches' blaze, not Ren Guang's flames; the repair corrects that misparse.

When the Xianzong heard of this, he promoted him to fengchaoqing, moved him to colonel of the left guard of the feathered guard, then general of the household rapid as tiger, then again to colonel of the long river.

When Xianzong heard of this, he promoted him to fengchaoqing, moved him to colonel of the left guard of the feathered guard, then general of the household rapid as tiger, and finally colonel of the Changshui Regiment.
長水 is the established regiment name Changshui, not the geographic phrase “Chang River.”

The Shizu heard and praised him, saying to Zhong: "Now my troops are already formed; the general may return to save his old mother, wife, and children—you should yourself recruit officials and people who can recover family members, grant a thousand million cash, and come take it from me."

Shizu heard and praised him, saying to Zhong, "Now my troops are formed. You may return to rescue your mother, wife, and children. Recruit officials and commoners capable of recovering your family; I will grant ten million cash—come and collect it from me."
The ruler promises the ten million cash; the previous syntax incorrectly made Li Zhong grant it.
He was again made left attendant-in-ordinary in the Office of the Censorate and often followed on campaigns.
He was again made Left Cao Palace Attendant and often followed on campaigns.
復為左曹侍中 is Left Cao palace attendant (侍中), not a Censorate (御史臺) post; the before invents the wrong office.
He was again made left attendant-in-ordinary in the Office of the Censorate and often followed on campaigns.
He was again made Left Cao palace attendant and often followed on campaigns.
Same office error on the literal line: 左曹侍中 is palace attendant under the Left Section, not an Office of the Censorate post.
The Shizu thereupon stayed at Zhending and took Empress Guo, who afterward was Yang's niece; for that reason he bound him with this.
The Shizu thereupon stayed at Zhending and took Empress Guo, who was Yang's niece; for that reason he bound him with this.
In 納郭后，後即揚之甥也, 後 resumes 郭后 ('the empress was Yang's niece'), not a temporal 'afterward'; the before makes the kinship nonsense.

He feasted Liu Yang and his generals at the Guo family house in Qili; Liu Yang struck the chime-sticks in merriment, then joined the advance that stormed Handan and finished the pacification of Hebei.

Guangwu then feasted Liu Yang and the generals at the Guo residence in Qili. Liu Yang played the zhu in celebration; Guangwu was thereby able to advance and capture Handan, and Liu Zhi accompanied him in pacifying Hebei.
築 is the zhu instrument; the final 從平河北 resumes the biographical subject Liu Zhi, not Guangwu.
Liu Xiang's fief shifted to Dongwuyang; his son Liu Shu succeeded but lost the title in Yongping 15 for plotting with Prince Ying of Chu.
Liu Xiang's fief shifted to Dongwuyang; when he died, his son Liu Shu succeeded, and in Yongping 15 Shu lost the title for plotting with Prince Ying of Chu.
向徙封東武陽侯，卒，子述嗣…國除 records Xiang's death before Shu's succession and Shu's attainder; the before omits 卒 and can blur who lost the fief.
He galloped riders to report white to the Shizu.
He dispatched mounted messengers at speed to report to Emperor Guangwu.
馳騎 means dispatching mounted messengers at speed; “galloped riders” is not natural English.
The Shizu said: "Great troops cannot move by night; therefore I did not rescue each other.
The Shizu said: "Great troops cannot move by night; therefore I did not come to your rescue.
故不相救耳: 相 marks the other party (Chun), so Guangwu says he did not come to the rescue—not a reciprocal 'rescue each other'.
He struck Liu Yong at Jiyin and took Dingtao below.
He struck Liu Yong at Jiyin and took Dingtao.
下定陶 means he took/captured Dingtao; appending 'below' wrongly literalizes the verb 下.
He followed in striking Dong Xian; passing through Dongjun, several thousand old and young of the common people followed the eastern carriage weeping, saying, "We wish again to obtain Lord Geng."
He followed in striking Dong Xian; passing through Dongjun, several thousand old and young of the common people followed the imperial carriage weeping, saying, "We wish again to obtain Lord Geng."
隨東駕涕泣: 東駕 is the imperial carriage/train, not an 'eastern' carriage.
Chun declined and went to his state; the Emperor said: "Wen Di said to Zhou Bo, 'The chancellor is what I esteem; you for me lead the marquises to their states'—now it is likewise."
Chun took leave to go to his state; the Emperor said: "Wen Di said to Zhou Bo, 'The chancellor is what I esteem; you for me lead the marquises to their states'—now it is likewise."
純辭就國 is the set phrase for taking leave to proceed to one's fief (then 受詔而去), not declining an offer.
In the thirteenth year he died in office; his posthumous title was marquis of Cheng.
In the thirteenth year he died in office; his posthumous title was Marquis Cheng.
English title order is Marquis Cheng; 成 is the posthumous name attached to the marquisate.

In the spring of the second year of Jianwu he sent Colonel of Cavalry Chen Fu and General Who Roams to Attack Deng Long to summon Yang; Yang closed the city gates and would not admit Fu and the others.
In the spring of the second year of Jianwu, Guangwu sent Cavalry Commandant Chen Fu and Roaming-Attack General Deng Long to summon Liu Yang; Liu Yang shut the gates and refused to admit them.
The refusal to admit Chen Fu and the others confirms that 征揚 here means summoning Liu Yang, not campaigning against him.
Easy paced the returning army on which two guardians it leaned.
The returning army moved at ease, relying on the two governors.
二守 refers to the two governors, not generic guardians, and 委佗 describes the returning army’s ease.
